title: fix: Home button stops opening after a failed run
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: clicking the Home icon does not open Home when session attention replaces the icon with a warning, question, or approval indicator. Stale child-failure details can also make the navigation button look like an unrelated error.

## User Impact

User impact: Home stays recognizable and clickable regardless of session failures. Run/queued/unread activity and draft/outbox badges remain; session attention keeps its existing session and Inbox surfaces. No configuration or data migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The generic session-row renderer puts an interactive attention tooltip inside the Home button. That tooltip stops click propagation. Home now uses the existing noninteractive session glyph directly rather than embedding a competing action. This complements the child-failure aggregation fix in #188309.

## Evidence

- Production-bundle regression: both saved-layout cases fail on base `66004e076d4dcfb7e6d1ff14c1a894a03f475908` after a real click on the failed Home glyph, waiting for Home chat; both pass with this fix, including a message sent to the Home session.
- Home context suite: 3/3 pass in 3.90 seconds; desktop/touch rail alignment: 2/2 pass. Combined invocation: 26.78 seconds including the production UI build.
- Existing sidebar interactions/footer tests: 77/77 pass (22.76-second invocation); rail tests: 34/34 pass (8.81-second invocation).
- UI TypeScript, scoped oxlint, oxfmt, and diff checks pass.
- Independent local autoreview, P0–P2, of the complete candidate against the base above: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable; ClawSweeper has acknowledged the PR; its hosted review is pending.
- Simplification: removes the generic session-row attention/action machinery from Home, with no new state owner. Production delta +11 lines; test delta +8 lines extends existing flows, with an exact 8-line regression allocation. Existing reactive effects/listeners and ownership APIs are unchanged.

Browser proof uses synthetic Gateway fixtures and the real production UI bundle, not a live provider. The completed [CI run 41072397196](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41072397196) accounts for 8,004 job-seconds (summed job execution, not billing): 32 jobs succeeded, 26 skipped, and the mobile-menu UI job plus its aggregate gate failed.

### CI qualification

The sole root failure is `chat-header-session-menu-mobile.test.tsx` / `copies through the native action and closes the whole mobile menu`, in the unchanged first-case DOM-readiness poll before Copy is selected. On the exact CI baseline `fa286a72d3624be71e65165404ef66eb013b24d2`, a controlled pinned-Bun probe reproduces that assertion while the real lazy menu-content exports are held; releasing those same exports makes the control appear. The menu/test/readiness inputs are byte-identical in the actual tested merge `fa4421c8d77a9c64377c4e9653be9c63441b00e9`. The changed Home renderer is not mounted by that standalone fixture.

The unchanged original file passes the focused pinned-Bun replay (15/15, 2.82-second invocation), which is not claimed as a repair. This is independently attributed to the existing cold-import fixture deadline, not a full replay of CI scheduling. Native inherited-failure admission retains the failed CI and enforces all other security/review checks. No CI rerun, retry, skip, timeout increase, or unrelated production change is used.
